cohort: The study included 94 women with postdated pregnancies, comparing outcomes between those who underwent induced labor and those who experienced spontaneous labor.
finding: Induced labor in postdated pregnancies was associated with increased incidences of adverse maternal outcomes (oligohydramnios, meconium-stained amniotic fluid, emergency lower segment cesarean section, postpartum hemorrhage, infection) and worse neonatal outcomes (NICU hospitalizations, low birth weight).
mod_finding: Induced labor correlated with an increased incidence of emergency lower segment cesarean section.
